title: Russia's Sber plans USDT and Ether loans under new regulated crypto framework
dek: Sber, Russia's largest bank, will expand Bitcoin-collateralized lending to include USDT and Ether after regulators cleared the assets for public trading. The move signals institutional crypto adoption in a sanctioned economy and raises questions about demand for Russia's own digital currency.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Sber plans to accept USDT and Ether as loan collateral alongside Bitcoin following regulatory clearance for public crypto trading.
bottom_line: Watch for Sber's formal announcement of loan terms, collateral ratios, and launch timing. The move also leaves open whether Russia's regulatory stance reflects genuine demand for stablecoin access or signals about the competitive position of its own digital currency projects.
body: Russia's largest bank Sber is expanding its crypto lending program to include USDT and Ether, according to Cointelegraph's reporting. The expansion follows regulatory clearance for public crypto trading under a new Russian framework.

Sber had previously accepted Bitcoin as loan collateral. The planned addition of the stablecoin and Ethereum signals institutional appetite for crypto assets in a major economy operating under Western sanctions.

Cointelegraph's report does not specify a timeline for the expansion, collateral ratios, loan terms, interest rates, or implementation stages. The mechanics of how Sber will handle compliance with sanctions regimes on USDT transactions, a USD-pegged stablecoin, remain unaddressed in available reporting.
